deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is a short handwritten notice in German, a lecture announcement of the kind posted at Göttingen, written in the lower half of a folded sheet. Translation: 'I will begin my lecture on the mathematical theory of gravity, electricity and magnetism as soon as a sufficient number of auditors have registered. Göttingen, 30 April 1860. B. Riemann (Sternwarte).' The address 'Sternwarte' is the Göttingen observatory, where Riemann had lodgings after succeeding Dirichlet in 1859. The context fits. The previous page is a Latin/German catalogue announcement of a five-hour-per-week course on partial differential equations with physical applications. The next page is a library or loan note for Riess, 'Die Lehre von der Reibungselektricität' (2 vols., Berlin 1853), signed by Riemann. That book is a natural reference for an electrostatics course. Riemann's lectures on this subject were later edited by Hattendorff as 'Schwere, Elektricität und Magnetismus' (Hannover 1876). That edition is usually associated with his course of summer semester 1861. This notice shows that the course was announced for summer semester 1860, conditional on enrolment. There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct.

results.what: Announcement of a lecture course on the mathematical theory of gravity, electricity and magnetism (potential theory and its physical applications), Göttingen, summer semester 1860, to begin once enough students have enrolled.
results.modern_name: Lecture course on potential theory / mathematical physics (published posthumously as 'Schwere, Elektricität und Magnetismus', ed. K. Hattendorff, 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative lecture notice with no mathematical content. Riemann's lectures on gravity, electricity and magnetism are well known through Hattendorff's 1876 edition. The only minor detail is the dated, conditional announcement of the course for summer 1860, alongside his residence at the observatory. That is of slight biographical interest only.

The rest of the transcription (Vorlesung, mathematische Theorie der Schwere, genügende Anzahl von Zuhörern, Göttingen den 30. April 1860, B. Riemann, (Sternwarte)) agrees with the image.
